\par\vspace{2pt}\footnotesize\textit{Preliminary observations (to verify):}
\begin{itemize}\setlength{\itemsep}{0pt}\setlength{\parskip}{0pt}
  \item \textbf{DP hybrid (\texttt{split}, $k>0$) pays off most consistently} --- it helps both SAGE and GAT, and the speedup \emph{grows with} $k$: the largest interior $k$ ($k{=}L{-}1$) is the fastest hybrid in 13 of 18 cells. Largest gains are on \textbf{PCIe + deep/wide} (SAGE PCIe $L{=}4$: $+34\%$).
  \item \textbf{Pipeline hybrid pays off for SAGE but OOMs for GAT.} For SAGE, \texttt{pipe}/\texttt{pipe+DP} beat baseline in most cells ($+4\%$ to $+20\%$). For GAT, \emph{all 30} pipeline cells ran out of memory on papers100M at these sizes (recorded as OOM, kept in place).
  \item \textbf{Gains track communication pressure} --- PCIe $>$ NVLink and deeper/wider $>$ shallow, i.e. the hybrids help most exactly where the shuffle/all-to-all dominates. (Preliminary; to verify.)
\end{itemize}
